Low/normal FSH + low estrogen → hypothalamic/pituitary cause; persistent unexplained prolactin elevation → pituitary MRI
POI before 40: ≥4 months irregular/absent cycles with FSH >25 IU/L; repeat if uncertain
Post-instrumentation amenorrhea with otherwise normal endocrine testing → saline sonography/hysteroscopy for adhesions

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Functional hypothalamic → **restore energy intake**, reduce excessive exercise, address eating disorder/stress
Prolactinoma → cabergoline; thyroid disease → correct thyroid function; Asherman → hysteroscopic adhesiolysis
★ POI → **estrogen replacement plus progestogen if uterus present**, usually until natural menopause age
Chronic anovulation → endometrial protection with cyclic progestogen or combined contraception; treat underlying cause

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypoestrogenism → infertility, low bone density; prolonged unopposed estrogen → endometrial hyperplasia
Absent uterus differs from absent ovaries: fertility options depend on anatomy and gonadal function

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate nutrition, avoid overtraining/uterine injury; intermittent ovulation still requires contraception

rows.label: Mimics
items: Imperforate hymen: cyclic pain, bulging bluish hymen, hematocolpos
PCOS: hyperandrogenism with chronic anovulation, estrogen generally preserved

amniotic-fluid-disorders.name: Amniotic fluid disorders
amniotic-fluid-disorders.scope: Oligohydramnios (AFI <= 5 cm or single deepest pocket < 2 cm, renal anomalies, uteroplacental insufficiency), polyhydramnios (AFI >= 24 cm, maternal diabetes, GI atresia, twin-twin transfusion syndrome, anencephaly)
amniotic-fluid-disorders.core: Amniotic fluid reflects fetal urine production and swallowing; abnormal volume directs evaluation toward membrane rupture, placental disease, or fetal anomalies.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Low fluid: PPROM, post-term pregnancy, maternal vascular disease, ACE inhibitors, NSAIDs
High fluid: maternal diabetes, esophageal/duodenal atresia, anencephaly, fetal anemia; many mild cases idiopathic
Monochorionic twins: donor oligohydramnios and recipient polyhydramnios suggest twin-twin transfusion

rows.label: Clues
items: Fundal height smaller/larger than dates; fluid extremes may alter fetal movement perception
Severe excess → maternal dyspnea, distended tense abdomen; low volume → recurrent variable decelerations

rows.label: Pathophys
items: After midgestation, urine supplies most fluid; swallowing removes it
Placental hypoperfusion or absent kidneys reduces input; impaired swallowing or osmotic diuresis increases volume

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Ultrasound fluid measurement** plus anatomy survey; single deepest pocket reduces oligohydramnios overdiagnosis
Low volume → sterile speculum examination for rupture, assess kidneys/bladder, growth and umbilical Doppler
High volume → diabetes testing, detailed fetal anatomy; evaluate anemia/infection when suggested

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Isolated persistent oligohydramnios → surveillance and delivery at **36–37+6 weeks**, or diagnosis thereafter
Low fluid from PPROM/FGR → manage underlying cause; intrapartum recurrent variables may benefit from amnioinfusion
★ Severe symptomatic polyhydramnios → **amnioreduction**; indomethacin not solely for fluid reduction
Mild idiopathic polyhydramnios → spontaneous term labor; elective induction no earlier than 39 weeks

rows.label: Complications
items: Early prolonged severe low fluid → pulmonary hypoplasia, limb contractures; later → cord compression
Excess fluid → preterm labor, malpresentation, prolapsed cord, abruption after decompression, postpartum atony

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Optimize glucose control; avoid **ACE inhibitors** and nonessential NSAIDs during pregnancy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Macrosomia: large fundal height but normal fluid measurement
Incorrect dating: size discrepancy without true volume abnormality

amniotic-fluid-disorders.evidence: Polyhydramnios checked 2026-10-30: [SMFM Consult 46](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30048635/); oligohydramnios timing follows established ACOG guidance.

antepartum-bleeding.name: Antepartum bleeding
antepartum-bleeding.scope: Placenta previa, placental abruption, vasa previa, uterine rupture, transabdominal ultrasound before digital exam, Kleihauer-Betke test, emergent cesarean delivery
antepartum-bleeding.core: Bleeding in later pregnancy requires immediate maternal stabilization and fetal assessment, followed by placental localization before any digital cervical examination.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Previa: prior cesarean, multiparity; abruption: hypertension, cocaine, trauma, prior abruption
Vasa previa: velamentous cord, accessory placental lobe, IVF; rupture: uterine scar, obstructed labor

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Shock may exceed visible blood loss** with concealed abruption or internal hemorrhage
Assess uterine tone, pain, contractions, fetal tracing, membrane status; bleeding volume alone is unreliable

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Maternal placental bleeding versus fetal vessel hemorrhage; vasa previa can rapidly exsanguinate fetus
Placental separation or uterine disruption compromises oxygen delivery independent of maternal external blood loss

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ CBC, type/crossmatch, coagulation studies including fibrinogen; continuous fetal monitoring if viable
★ **Ultrasound before digital examination**; transvaginal imaging safely clarifies placenta–cervix relationship
Normal ultrasound does not exclude abruption; suspected rupture is a clinical emergency
Rh-negative bleeding/trauma → Kleihauer–Betke or flow cytometry quantifies fetomaternal hemorrhage for anti-D dosing

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ ABCs, two large IVs, blood products when needed; **do not delay delivery for imaging if unstable**
Hemorrhage/fetal compromise → emergency cesarean; rupture → laparotomy, uterine repair or hysterectomy
Stable preterm previa → observation, pelvic rest, corticosteroids when eligible; planned cesarean before labor
Abruption: deliver if significant or compromised; vaginal birth possible when stable and imminent or fetal demise
Unsensitized Rh-negative patient → anti-D immunoglobulin; correct abruption-associated coagulopathy

rows.label: Complications
items: Hemorrhagic shock, DIC, AKI, hysterectomy; fetal hypoxia, death, prematurity
Previa plus cesarean scar increases placenta accreta spectrum risk and operative hemorrhage

rows.label: Prevention
items: Control BP, avoid cocaine/tobacco; prenatal placental/cord localization and planned high-risk delivery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Bloody show: small mucus-streaked bleeding with cervical change
Cervical lesion: contact bleeding, visible source on speculum examination

table.title: Critical distinctions
rows: Bleeding after rupture; sudden fetal bradycardia
Scarred uterus; lost station, fetal bradycardia

antepartum-bleeding.evidence: Not checked online; established obstetric hemorrhage teaching.

appendicitis.name: Appendicitis
appendicitis.scope: Acute appendicitis, clinical presentation, pediatric and pregnancy considerations, imaging (ultrasound, CT), surgical management
appendicitis.core: Periumbilical pain migrating to the right lower quadrant, followed by anorexia and nausea, suggests appendiceal inflammation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Adolescents/young adults; luminal obstruction by lymphoid hyperplasia or fecalith
Older adults may have obstructing neoplasm; immunosuppression can blunt findings

rows.label: Clues
items: McBurney tenderness, guarding, fever; Rovsing, psoas, or obturator signs depend on position
★ **Diffuse peritonitis, toxicity, hypotension** → perforation/sepsis until proven otherwise
Young children: nonspecific symptoms and rapid progression; pregnancy: displaced appendix, less reliable examination

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Luminal obstruction → distention, venous congestion, bacterial invasion → ischemia/perforation
Visceral midgut pain precedes focal parietal peritoneal irritation

rows.label: Dx
items: CBC, urinalysis, **pregnancy test** in reproductive-age patients; pyuria does not exclude appendicitis
★ Stable nonpregnant adult → **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast** when diagnosis uncertain
★ Child/pregnancy → **ultrasound first**; nondiagnostic → MRI without gadolinium, or CT in nonpregnant child
Noncompressible enlarged appendix >6 mm with periappendiceal inflammation supports diagnosis
Clear peritonitis → surgical evaluation; do not delay necessary operation for repeated imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ NPO, **IV fluids, analgesia, ceftriaxone + metronidazole**, surgical consultation
Laparoscopic appendectomy definitive; do not withhold necessary surgery during pregnancy
Selected uncomplicated cases → antibiotics after shared decision; recurrence/failure higher, especially with appendicolith
Localized abscess/phlegmon in stable patient → antibiotics ± image-guided drainage; follow-up based on age/risk

rows.label: Complications
items: Perforation, abscess, peritonitis, sepsis, ileus
Postoperative wound infection, intra-abdominal collection, adhesional obstruction

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: positive hCG, adnexal findings
Ovarian torsion: sudden unilateral pelvic pain; gastroenteritis: diarrhea prominent before diffuse cramping
Mesenteric adenitis: viral prodrome, normal appendix on imaging

appendicitis.evidence: Not checked online; established general-surgery evaluation and treatment principles.

benign-breast-conditions.name: Benign breast conditions
benign-breast-conditions.scope: Fibroadenoma, fibrocystic changes, intraductal papilloma, breast cyst, fat necrosis, galactocele, breast abscess
benign-breast-conditions.core: Breast symptoms require age-directed imaging and clinical–radiologic concordance; a benign-appearing examination alone cannot exclude malignancy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Reproductive hormonal cycling; lactation and milk stasis; breast trauma or prior surgery
Smoking predisposes to recurrent subareolar abscess

rows.label: Clues
items: Galactocele: painless postlactational mass; fat–fluid level on imaging
Abscess: focal tender erythematous fluctuant mass, sometimes fever; often Staphylococcus aureus
★ Spontaneous unilateral **bloody single-duct discharge** → papilloma or malignancy evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hormone-responsive stromal/glandular tissue produces cyclic changes; duct obstruction causes retained secretions
Adipose injury causes inflammatory necrosis and calcification that can resemble cancer

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Palpable mass **<30 years → ultrasound**; ≥30 → diagnostic mammography with targeted ultrasound
Suspicious solid lesion or imaging–exam discordance → **core needle biopsy**
Simple cyst: anechoic, thin-walled, posterior enhancement; no solid component
Nonlactational abscess or persistent inflammation after antibiotics → exclude underlying carcinoma

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Simple painful cyst → aspiration; bloody fluid or residual mass → further tissue evaluation
Fibroadenoma → observe when concordant; excise if rapidly enlarging, large or symptomatic
Fibrocystic pain → supportive bra, topical/oral NSAID; galactocele → aspiration if symptomatic
★ Abscess → ultrasound-guided drainage + **dicloxacillin/cephalexin**; MRSA risk → clindamycin
Continue breastfeeding/pumping with lactational infection; persistent pathologic discharge → breast surgical evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent periductal abscess → fistula; incomplete drainage → persistent infection
Proliferative lesions with atypia increase future cancer risk; simple cysts do not

rows.label: Prevention
items: Effective breast emptying during lactation; smoking cessation for recurrent periductal disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cancer: irregular fixed mass, retraction or suspicious nodes
Phyllodes: rapidly enlarging fibroepithelial mass requiring excision

benign-breast-conditions.evidence: Not checked online; established breast diagnostic principles.

bladder-cancer.name: Bladder cancer
bladder-cancer.scope: Urothelial (transitional cell) carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, painless gross hematuria, smoking and occupational exposures, cystoscopy, transurethral resection
bladder-cancer.core: Painless gross hematuria in an older adult requires evaluation for urinary tract malignancy, even during anticoagulation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ **Smoking**, aromatic amines in dye/rubber industries; older age and male sex
Cyclophosphamide, pelvic radiation; chronic catheter irritation and Schistosoma haematobium predispose to squamous carcinoma

rows.label: Clues
items: Intermittent bleeding, clots; carcinoma in situ may produce irritative voiding symptoms without a visible mass
Advanced disease: pelvic pain, hydronephrosis, weight loss, or bone pain

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Urothelial field injury → multifocal tumors and recurrence throughout the collecting system
Squamous metaplasia from chronic inflammation → keratinizing malignancy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Cystoscopy + CT urography** evaluate bladder and upper tracts; urinalysis/culture assess alternatives
Urine cytology helps detect high-grade disease/CIS; negative cytology does not exclude cancer
★ **TURBT including muscularis propria** establishes histology, grade, and depth
T1 disease → repeat resection within 6 weeks; invasive disease → chest/abdomen/pelvis staging

rows.label: Tx
items: Clot retention → large-bore catheter, irrigation; persistent obstruction or bleeding → urgent urology
Selected fit patients seeking bladder preservation → maximal resection plus concurrent chemoradiation
Avoid intravesical chemotherapy with suspected bladder perforation; BCG contraindicated during active symptomatic UTI

rows.label: Complications
items: Obstructive renal failure, recurrent hemorrhage, nodal or distant metastases
Intravesical BCG → cystitis; rarely disseminated infection; cystectomy → diversion-related metabolic complications

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation and occupational protection; no routine population screening
★ **Surveillance cystoscopy** after treatment because recurrence is common; interval based on risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Nephrolithiasis: colicky flank pain, stone on noncontrast CT
Glomerulonephritis: dysmorphic RBCs, RBC casts, proteinuria
Cystitis: dysuria and positive culture; persistent hematuria after treatment still needs evaluation

table.title: Depth determines definitive treatment
rows: TURBT + intravesical BCG; selected early cystectomy

breast-cancer-screening.name: Breast cancer screening
breast-cancer-screening.scope: USPSTF screening mammography recommendations, age-based intervals, high-risk screening (BRCA, prior chest radiation, breast MRI), clinical breast exam, diagnostic evaluation of abnormal screening
breast-cancer-screening.core: USPSTF recommends biennial mammography from ages 40–74 for average-risk women; symptoms require diagnostic evaluation regardless of screening schedule.

rows.label: Who
items: Average risk includes family history or dense breasts without a defined high-risk syndrome
★ BRCA pathogenic variant, young chest irradiation or lifetime risk **≥20–25%** → high-risk pathway

rows.label: Start/stop
items: Age ≥75: insufficient USPSTF evidence; individualize by health, life expectancy and preference
High risk: annual MRI plus mammography, typically around age 30; specialist-tailored earlier MRI

rows.label: Test
items: ★ Digital mammography/tomosynthesis; **MRI supplements**, not replaces, high-risk mammography
Clinical breast examination and breast self-examination do not substitute for imaging

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ BI-RADS 0 → **diagnostic views/targeted ultrasound**; 4–5 → core needle biopsy
BI-RADS 3 → short-interval imaging, usually 6 months; 1–2 → routine interval
Palpable concerning mass with negative imaging → tissue assessment for clinical–radiologic discordance

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Older USPSTF teaching began routine screening at 50; **2024 update starts at 40**
Dense breasts alone: insufficient USPSTF evidence for routine supplemental ultrasound/MRI
Harms: false positives, biopsy, overdiagnosis; concerning mass needs evaluation despite normal mammogram

breast-neoplasia.name: Breast neoplasia
breast-neoplasia.scope: Ductal carcinoma in situ, invasive ductal and lobular carcinoma, receptor status (ER, PR, HER2), metastatic disease (bone, visceral), surgical management, endocrine and chemotherapy
breast-neoplasia.core: A suspicious breast lesion requires core biopsy, assessment of invasion and ER/PR/HER2 status to guide local and systemic treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, BRCA-related syndromes, family history, prior chest irradiation
Prolonged estrogen exposure, postmenopausal obesity, alcohol; atypical proliferative breast lesions

rows.label: Clues
items: Painless hard irregular mass, skin/nipple retraction, unilateral bloody discharge or axillary node
★ Peau d’orange, diffuse erythema and edema → **inflammatory breast cancer**, even without discrete mass
Persistent unilateral eczematous nipple lesion → Paget disease; investigate underlying carcinoma

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Invasion through basement membrane enables lymphatic/hematogenous metastasis
ER/PR signaling and HER2 amplification create actionable tumor drivers; triple-negative tumors lack these targets

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Diagnostic mammography + targeted ultrasound** → core needle biopsy of suspicious lesion
Pathology: invasion, grade, **ER/PR/HER2**; assess regional nodes clinically and with targeted imaging
Clinically node-negative invasive disease → sentinel node biopsy during definitive surgery
Distant staging scans for advanced disease or suspicious symptoms; not every small asymptomatic cancer

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Early: lumpectomy + radiation or mastectomy; locally advanced: neoadjuvant systemic treatment then surgery/radiation
ER-positive → tamoxifen or postmenopausal aromatase inhibitor; chemotherapy based on stage/biology
★ HER2-positive → **trastuzumab-based** treatment; monitor LVEF
Triple-negative → chemotherapy; selected higher-risk disease → pembrolizumab-containing regimen
Bone metastases → **zoledronate/denosumab**; systemic treatment by receptors, chemotherapy for visceral crisis

rows.label: Complications
items: Metastases to bone, lung, liver, brain; surgery/radiation → lymphedema
Tamoxifen → VTE/endometrial cancer; aromatase inhibitors → bone loss; trastuzumab → cardiomyopathy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Age/risk-based screening, genetic counseling for suggestive pedigree; selected high-risk patients → chemoprevention
BRCA-related very high risk → discuss risk-reducing surgery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Mastitis: lactation-associated tenderness/fever, improves with antibiotics
Fat necrosis: trauma/surgery history; biopsy if discordant imaging

table.title: Histologic distinctions
rows: Bilateral risk marker; discohesive lobular cells

breast-neoplasia.evidence: Not checked online; established breast-oncology management principles.

cervical-cancer-screening.name: Cervical Cancer Screening
cervical-cancer-screening.scope: USPSTF guidelines by age (Pap smear alone 21-29, Pap with hrHPV cotesting or hrHPV alone 30-65), screening cessation, post-hysterectomy
cervical-cancer-screening.core: Screen average-risk people with a cervix from age 21; age, prior results, and cervical precancer history determine testing and cessation.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ **Average-risk cervix present**; sexual history and HPV vaccination do not alter schedule
HIV, immunosuppression, DES exposure, prior CIN 2+ → separate surveillance pathways

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Stop after 65 only with **adequate negative prior screening** and no high-risk history
Adequate: 3 negative cytology/2 HPV-based tests over 10 years; latest within 5
Total benign hysterectomy, no CIN 2+/cancer → stop; supracervical hysterectomy → continue

rows.label: Test
items: Choose one age-specific strategy below; annual testing increases unnecessary procedures

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ **HPV 16/18 or high-grade cytology → colposcopy**; other results use prior-history risk assessment
CIN 2+ treatment → HPV-based surveillance at least 25 years, even beyond 65

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Postcoital bleeding or visible lesion → diagnostic evaluation**, regardless of screening interval
Under 21: no routine screening; unknown/inadequate history after 65 → continue
USPSTF 2018 final schedule below; later draft self-collection proposals do not replace final guidance

table.title: USPSTF age-based choices
rows: Primary hrHPV or cotest every 5 years

cervical-cancer-screening.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [USPSTF final recommendation (2018)](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/cervical-cancer-screening); post-treatment surveillance follows established ASCCP teaching.

cervical-neoplasia.name: Cervical neoplasia
cervical-neoplasia.scope: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, invasive cervical cancer, squamous cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, colposcopy
cervical-neoplasia.core: Persistent high-risk HPV drives cervical precancer and cancer; abnormal screening needs risk-based evaluation, while visible symptomatic lesions require biopsy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: HPV 16/18 persistence, smoking, HIV/immunosuppression, limited screening access

rows.label: Clues
items: CIN usually asymptomatic; invasive disease → postcoital/intermenstrual bleeding, watery discharge
Friable cervical mass, pelvic pain; hydronephrosis or leg edema suggests advanced spread

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Viral E6 degrades p53; E7 inactivates Rb → transformation-zone dysplasia
Squamous carcinoma most common; adenocarcinoma arises in endocervical glands

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Visible lesion → biopsy**, regardless of prior normal Pap/HPV result
★ HPV 16/18 positivity, ASC-H or AGC → **colposcopy**, even with otherwise reassuring screening
AGC → endocervical sampling; add endometrial biopsy at ≥35 or with endometrial risk factors
Colposcopy-directed biopsy diagnoses CIN; invasive cancer → pelvic examination, MRI/PET-CT for extent
Pregnancy → risk-based colposcopy; no endocervical curettage or expedited excision

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ CIN 3 → **excisional treatment** outside pregnancy; CIN 2 may be observed with fertility concerns
CIN 1 → observation; select nonpregnant patients ≥25 with very high risk → expedited excision
AIS → diagnostic excision; hysterectomy after childbearing if margins adequately assessed
Selected microinvasive cancer → conization; other early invasive disease → hysterectomy
Locally advanced → cisplatin-based chemoradiation plus brachytherapy

rows.label: Complications
items: Ureteral obstruction, fistulas, metastases; cervical excision increases subsequent preterm-birth risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **HPV vaccination** plus age-based screening; vaccination does not eliminate screening
After treated CIN 2/3/AIS: initial intensive HPV surveillance, then every 3 years for ≥25 years

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cervicitis: mucopurulent discharge and positive STI testing
Endometrial cancer: uterine-source bleeding; benign ectropion: smooth eversion without destructive lesion

table.title: Histologic grade
rows: More than two-thirds; basement membrane intact

cervicitis-pid.name: Cervicitis and pelvic inflammatory disease
cervicitis-pid.core: Sexually active patient with mucopurulent discharge or postcoital bleeding; ascending infection adds pelvic pain, sometimes an adnexal abscess.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age <25, new/multiple partners, inconsistent condoms, prior STI
IUD-associated PID risk concentrated within first 3 weeks after insertion

rows.label: Clues
items: Cervical friability, easily induced endocervical bleeding; infection sometimes asymptomatic
Dyspareunia, fever; severe unilateral pain/adnexal mass → **tubo-ovarian abscess**
Peritonitis, shock → rupture; RUQ pain → Fitz-Hugh–Curtis perihepatitis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: GC/CT ascend cervix → endometrium/tubes; PID often polymicrobial, including anaerobes

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pregnancy test** first; vaginal/cervical or urine **GC/CT NAAT**; HIV/syphilis testing
★ Pelvic pain + **cervical motion, uterine, OR adnexal tenderness** → presumptive PID; no confirmation delay
Negative cervical NAAT does not exclude upper-tract infection; normal discharge/no vaginal leukocytes argues against PID
**Transvaginal US** for abscess or diagnostic uncertainty; routine laparoscopy unnecessary

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Cervicitis: empiric GC/CT coverage IF high risk/unreliable follow-up; otherwise await NAAT
★ Admit IF **pregnant, abscess, severe illness**, oral intolerance, uncertain surgical diagnosis, or failure by 72 h
Abscess rupture → emergency surgery; persistent abscess after 48–72 h antibiotics → drainage
Pregnant chlamydia → **azithromycin**, avoid doxycycline; retain IUD initially, reassess if no improvement

rows.label: Complications
items: Tubal infertility, ectopic pregnancy, chronic pelvic pain; abscess → sepsis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Treat partners from prior **60 days**; abstain until courses completed, partners treated, symptoms resolved
Retest GC/CT at 3 months; pregnant chlamydia → test of cure at 4 weeks
Annual GC/CT screening: sexually active women <25, older women with risks; condoms

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: positive hCG, no confirmed intrauterine pregnancy
Ovarian torsion: abrupt unilateral pain, vomiting; Doppler flow may persist
Appendicitis: migrating RLQ pain, CT appendiceal inflammation

table.title: Antibiotic branches
rows: Ceftriaxone; add CT regimen unless excluded
Oral drugs 14 days; ceftriaxone once IM outpatient

chlamydia-infection.name: Chlamydia infection
chlamydia-infection.scope: Chlamydia trachomatis, nongonococcal urethritis, cervicitis, lymphogranuloma venereum, neonatal conjunctivitis and pneumonia, NAAT screening and diagnosis, doxycycline and azithromycin
chlamydia-infection.core: Often silent sexually transmitted intracellular infection causing urethritis or cervicitis; untreated infection threatens fertility and can infect newborns during delivery.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age <25 years, new/multiple partners, inconsistent condom use, infected partner; perinatal exposure

rows.label: Clues
items: Dysuria, scant discharge, sterile pyuria; friable cervix, mucopurulent discharge, postcoital bleeding
★ Neonatal conjunctivitis at **5–12 days**; afebrile staccato pneumonia at **1–3 months**
LGV: transient painless genital ulcer → tender inguinal nodes/buboes or invasive proctocolitis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: C. trachomatis: obligate intracellular bacterium; D–K serovars cause genital/perinatal infection, L1–L3 cause LGV

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **NAAT**: vaginal swab preferred in women; first-catch urine in men; rectal swab after exposure
Test for gonorrhea, HIV, syphilis; fever/pelvic pain → evaluate for PID
Infant conjunctival testing requires epithelial cells; nasopharyngeal testing for pneumonia
Sexually active MSM: annual site-specific screening; every 3–6 months with persistent high risk

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Uncomplicated infection → **doxycycline for 7 days**; LGV → 21 days
★ Pregnancy → **azithromycin**, single dose; alternative when adherence doubtful, less reliable for rectal infection
Neonatal disease → oral erythromycin for 14 days; azithromycin alternative; topical treatment alone inadequate
Gonorrhea suspected or detected → add ceftriaxone; PID requires broader multidrug coverage

rows.label: Complications
items: PID → tubal infertility, ectopic pregnancy, chronic pelvic pain; epididymitis, reactive arthritis
LGV → rectal strictures/fistulas; infant macrolides → hypertrophic pyloric stenosis risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Treat partners from preceding **60 days**; expedited partner treatment where legal
Abstain until 7-day course completed or 7 days after single dose, and partners treated
Annual screening: sexually active women <25 years, older women with risk; pregnancy entry screening, risk-based rescreening
Retest at 3 months; pregnancy test-of-cure at 4 weeks; neonatal eye ointment does not prevent chlamydia

rows.label: Mimics
items: Gonorrhea: often more purulent; organism-specific NAAT differentiates
M. genitalium: persistent nongonococcal urethritis after doxycycline; separate NAAT
HSV: painful ulcers and external dysuria rather than isolated cervical discharge

congenital-adrenal-hyperplasia.name: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia
congenital-adrenal-hyperplasia.core: Newborn salt loss or atypical genitalia demands adrenal evaluation; hypertension with abnormal puberty suggests a different steroid-synthesis block.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autosomal recessive inheritance; affected sibling, consanguinity
Classic disease presents neonatally; partial enzyme deficiency may present with adolescent androgen excess

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Neonatal vomiting, weight loss, dehydration, **shock** → salt-wasting adrenal crisis
46,XX virilization with internal female organs; 46,XY infants may lack obvious external warning signs
Nonclassic 21-hydroxylase deficiency: premature pubarche, hirsutism, acne or irregular menses

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Low cortisol removes feedback → ↑ACTH and adrenal hyperplasia
Steroid precursors accumulate upstream; androgen and mineralocorticoid effects depend on enzyme block

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **17-hydroxyprogesterone** screens for 21-hydroxylase deficiency; elevated values → confirmatory steroid testing
Borderline nonclassic disease → ACTH-stimulated 17-OHP; electrolytes, renin, cortisol and androgens guide subtype
Ambiguous genitalia → karyotype, pelvic ultrasound, endocrine consultation; avoid premature sex assignment
Newborn screen may miss milder disease; clinical instability overrides screening results

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Crisis → **IV hydrocortisone**, isotonic saline, dextrose; treat severe hyperkalemia
Glucocorticoid replacement suppresses ACTH; salt-wasting forms → fludrocortisone plus infant salt supplementation
11β/17α-associated hypertension → glucocorticoids; add antihypertensives for persistent elevation
Genital differences → multidisciplinary counseling; timing of surgery requires informed shared decisions

rows.label: Complications
items: Untreated crisis → death; androgen excess → precocious pseudopuberty, advanced bone age, short adult height
Excess replacement → growth suppression, obesity, osteoporosis; inadequate replacement → infertility/adrenal rest tumors

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Newborn screening, genetic counseling; emergency steroid kit, medical alert, illness/surgery stress dosing

rows.label: Mimics
items: Androgen insensitivity: 46,XY, testes, absent uterus, normal adrenal steroids
Pyloric stenosis: vomiting with hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis rather than salt-wasting hyperkalemia

congenital-adrenal-hyperplasia.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical teaching.

congenital-infections.name: Congenital infections
congenital-infections.scope: Cytomegalovirus (sensorineural hearing loss, periventricular calcifications), Toxoplasmosis (chorioretinitis), Parvovirus B19 (hydrops), Rubella, Varicella, Zika, screening and diagnosis
congenital-infections.core: Congenital infection causes growth restriction, hepatosplenomegaly, jaundice, thrombocytopenia, or hydrops; organ-specific patterns identify the pathogen.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: CMV: toddler saliva/urine; toxoplasma: undercooked meat, cat feces; B19: child with slapped-cheek rash
Absent rubella/varicella immunity; mosquito exposure or sexual transmission in Zika-risk areas

rows.label: Clues
items: Petechiae/blueberry-muffin lesions, abnormal fetal ultrasound; many infected newborns initially appear well
★ B19 hydrops: cardiomegaly, ascites, edema without red-cell alloantibodies

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Transplacental infection disrupts organogenesis; later exposure may cause inflammation or marrow suppression
Toxoplasma transmission increases with gestational age; earlier infection causes more severe injury

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Maternal exposure → pathogen-specific **IgG/IgM**, paired titers or avidity; isolated IgM needs confirmation
★ CMV newborn diagnosis: saliva PCR then confirm urine PCR **within 21 days**
Suspected fetal infection → targeted ultrasound, pathogen-specific amniotic-fluid PCR; B19 → serial MCA Doppler
Prenatal rubella IgG routinely; no universal US maternal CMV, toxoplasma, or B19 screening

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptomatic congenital CMV → **valganciclovir**, monitor CBC and liver tests
Congenital toxoplasmosis → pyrimethamine + sulfadiazine + leucovorin; maternal regimen depends on fetal infection
B19 severe fetal anemia → intrauterine transfusion; rubella/Zika structural injury → supportive care
Maternal varicella exposure without immunity → varicella-zoster immune globulin; maternal pneumonia → IV acyclovir

rows.label: Complications
items: Stillbirth, neurodevelopmental disability; delayed/progressive hearing loss requires longitudinal audiology

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Rubella/varicella vaccination before pregnancy or postpartum; **live vaccines contraindicated during pregnancy**
Handwashing after diapers; cook meat, avoid litter handling; mosquito precautions and Zika exposure counseling

rows.label: Mimics
items: Aneuploidy: abnormal genetic testing rather than pathogen testing
Rh disease: positive maternal antibody screen with fetal anemia

table.title: Discriminating congenital patterns
rows: Periventricular calcifications, microcephaly, sensorineural hearing loss
Severe microcephaly, subcortical calcifications, ocular abnormalities

congenital-infections.evidence: CMV testing checked 2026-10-30: [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/cytomegalovirus/hcp/clinical-overview/index.html); remaining pathogen patterns established teaching.

contraception.name: Contraception
contraception.scope: Combined oral contraceptives, progestin-only pills, implant, intrauterine devices, tubal sterilization
contraception.core: Choose contraception through shared decisions about efficacy, bleeding, reversibility, adherence, and estrogen-related vascular risk.

rows.label: Who
items: Anyone seeking pregnancy prevention; adolescents and nulliparous patients can use IUDs or implants

rows.label: Schedule
items: Pills daily; implants/IUDs provide years of protection; replacement interval depends on product
★ Emergency contraception ≤**5 days**: copper IUD/ulipristal; levonorgestrel pills sooner preferred

rows.label: Special groups
items: Breastfeeding or estrogen contraindication → progestin-only method or copper IUD
Current breast cancer → copper IUD; avoid hormonal methods
Progestin-only pills: daily timing crucial; norethindrone less forgiving than drospirenone

rows.label: Choice
items: Combined pills: suppress ovulation, improve acne/cramps, reduce endometrial/ovarian cancer risk
★ **LARC** minimizes adherence failures; condoms add STI protection
Tubal sterilization: permanent; counsel regret, alternatives, surgical risk, ectopic risk after failure

rows.label: Contraindications
items: ★ Estrogen: **migraine with aura, thrombophilia/high-risk VTE**, severe hypertension, early postpartum
Smoking age ≥35: combined methods usually avoid; ≥15 cigarettes/day → absolute contraindication
IUD: pregnancy, cervicitis/PID, distorted cavity; copper: also Wilson disease

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Same-day STI screening need not delay insertion without cervicitis; prior PID alone permits IUD
Sterilization: voluntary informed consent; no required partner approval, parity, or marital status
After ulipristal, wait 5 days before progestin; backup contraception needed after hormonal restart

dysmenorrhea.name: Dysmenorrhea
dysmenorrhea.scope: Primary dysmenorrhea, secondary dysmenorrhea (endometriosis, adenomyosis, cervical stenosis), hematometra, NSAIDs, combined oral contraceptives
dysmenorrhea.core: Painful menstruation: primary disease begins after ovulatory cycles develop; later-onset, progressive, or refractory pain suggests pelvic pathology.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Early menarche, heavy/prolonged flow, family history, smoking
Prior cervical excision/ablation → stenosis; endometriosis and adenomyosis produce secondary symptoms

rows.label: Clues
items: Suprapubic cramping radiating to back/thighs, nausea, diarrhea, headache
★ **Dyspareunia, abnormal bleeding, infertility**, or pain outside menses → secondary cause
Amenorrhea or scant flow after cervical procedure with cyclic pain → retained menstrual blood

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Progesterone withdrawal → endometrial prostaglandins → uterine hypercontractility and ischemia
Outflow obstruction traps blood in uterine cavity → hematometra

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Classic adolescent presentation without red flags → **clinical diagnosis**, no initial imaging
Sexual activity → pregnancy test; infection risks → gonorrhea/chlamydia NAAT
Secondary features → pelvic examination and **transvaginal ultrasound**; transabdominal imaging if needed
No improvement after 3–6 months despite adherence → investigate secondary disease, consider laparoscopy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **NSAIDs**, starting 1–2 days before expected bleeding through first 2–3 days
★ Inadequate response/contraception desired → **combined OCP** or progestin; continuous suppression may help
Heat, exercise; avoid NSAIDs with active ulcer disease or significant renal dysfunction
Treat underlying lesion; cervical stenosis with hematometra → cervical dilation/drainage

rows.label: Complications
items: School/work absence, sleep disturbance; untreated secondary disease may impair fertility
Analgesic adverse effects: GI bleeding, renal injury; estrogen-containing contraception → VTE risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: Track cycles and preempt pain; ongoing menstrual suppression reduces recurrence when pregnancy not desired

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: positive hCG, nonmenstrual bleeding, possible instability
PID: fever, mucopurulent discharge, cervical motion tenderness

table.title: Secondary patterns
rows: Posterior nodularity; ultrasound may be normal
Heavy bleeding, boggy uniformly enlarged uterus

dysmenorrhea.evidence: Not checked online; established adolescent gynecology and pelvic-pain teaching.

early-pregnancy-loss.name: Early pregnancy loss
early-pregnancy-loss.scope: Threatened abortion, inevitable abortion, incomplete abortion, complete abortion, missed abortion, anembryonic pregnancy
early-pregnancy-loss.core: First-trimester bleeding requires pregnancy location and viability assessment before labeling miscarriage or choosing expectant, medical, or surgical management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Embryonic aneuploidy most common; maternal age, prior losses, uterine anomalies, antiphospholipid syndrome

rows.label: Clues
items: Cramping, vaginal bleeding, passage of tissue; symptoms may be absent with retained nonviable pregnancy
★ Hypotension, syncope, peritoneal signs → **hemorrhage or ruptured ectopic**
Fever, uterine tenderness, foul discharge → septic abortion

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Embryonic/fetal demise or failed embryonic development → decidual separation and variable cervical dilation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Transvaginal ultrasound** plus quantitative β-hCG; CBC, blood type, pelvic examination
Definitive nonviability: CRL ≥7 mm without heartbeat or mean sac diameter ≥25 mm without embryo
Absent embryo/heartbeat on repeat: ≥11 days after yolk sac, ≥14 days after sac-only → nonviable
No intrauterine pregnancy → serial hCG/ultrasound; tissue passage alone cannot exclude ectopic

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Unstable, infected, or uncontrolled hemorrhage → **urgent uterine aspiration**; sepsis → IV broad-spectrum antibiotics
Confirmed stable loss → patient choice: observation, mifepristone followed by misoprostol, or aspiration
Threatened loss → expectant follow-up; bed rest does not prevent miscarriage
★ Rh-negative loss **≥12 weeks → RhIg**; ACOG now omits routine testing/prophylaxis before 12 weeks

rows.label: Complications
items: Retained products, infection, hemorrhage; intrauterine adhesions after instrumentation; grief/depression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking/alcohol avoidance, optimize diabetes; most isolated chromosomal losses unpreventable
Recurrent clinical losses → assess uterine anatomy, antiphospholipid antibodies and selected genetic causes

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: extrauterine implantation, adnexal mass/free fluid
Gestational trophoblastic disease: very high hCG, abnormal cystic intrauterine tissue

endometrial-cancer.name: Endometrial cancer
endometrial-cancer.scope: Endometrial hyperplasia, endometrioid adenocarcinoma, uterine sarcoma (leiomyosarcoma, carcinosarcoma, radiation risk), unopposed estrogen, biopsy, staging
endometrial-cancer.core: Postmenopausal bleeding warrants endometrial evaluation; chronic unopposed estrogen drives hyperplasia and endometrioid carcinoma.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Obesity, chronic anovulation/PCOS, nulliparity, early menarche, late menopause, estrogen without progestin
Tamoxifen, Lynch syndrome; prior pelvic radiation increases uterine sarcoma risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Abnormal uterine bleeding, watery/bloody discharge; pelvic pain or enlarged uterus with advanced disease
Growing postmenopausal uterine mass → consider sarcoma; growth rate alone cannot establish malignancy

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Atypical hyperplasia/endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia: premalignant lesion with frequent concurrent carcinoma
Serous/clear-cell cancers: aggressive, estrogen-independent; carcinosarcoma classified as high-grade carcinoma
Leiomyosarcoma: malignant myometrial smooth muscle, usually de novo rather than transformation of benign leiomyoma

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ AUB at **≥45 years**, or younger with persistent bleeding/estrogen risks → endometrial biopsy
★ ACOG 2026: most postmenopausal bleeding → **TVUS plus tissue sampling**
Classic ≤4 mm reassurance rule changed; persistent bleeding always requires histology, regardless of thickness
Insufficient/negative blind biopsy with continued symptoms → hysteroscopy-directed biopsy; Pap does not exclude disease
Surgical staging assesses myometrial/cervical invasion, nodes, extrauterine spread; sarcoma can escape endometrial sampling

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Operable carcinoma → **total hysterectomy + bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy**, sentinel-node assessment
Advanced/high-risk disease → stage-directed radiation and systemic treatment; carboplatin/paclitaxel commonly used
Suspected sarcoma → intact uterine removal; avoid uncontained morcellation

rows.label: Complications
items: Anemia, metastasis, recurrence; lymph-node surgery → lymphedema

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Weight management; add **progestin to systemic estrogen** when uterus intact; evaluate Lynch families

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vaginal atrophy: thin friable mucosa; malignancy still needs exclusion
Leiomyoma: usually premenopausal, well-circumscribed smooth-muscle mass

table.title: Hyperplasia
rows: Progestin, often levonorgestrel IUD; repeat sampling
Hysterectomy; selected fertility preservation: progestin + serial biopsies

endometrial-cancer.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG bleeding update 2026](https://www.acog.org/news/news-releases/2026/04/acog-publishes-updated-guidance-evaluation-postmenopausal-bleeding), [EIN consensus](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/clinical-consensus/articles/2023/09/management-of-endometrial-intraepithelial-neoplasia-or-atypical-endometrial-hyperplasia); other content established teaching.

endometriosis.name: Endometriosis
endometriosis.scope: Pelvic endometriosis, deep infiltrating endometriosis, endometrioma (chocolate cyst), uterosacral nodularity, cyclic pelvic pain, dyspareunia, laparoscopy, medical management
endometriosis.core: Reproductive-age patient with progressive cyclic pelvic pain, deep dyspareunia, and infertility from ectopic endometrial tissue.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Early menarche, short cycles, prolonged menstruation, family history; obstructed menstrual outflow

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Uterosacral nodularity**, fixed retroverted uterus, posterior cul-de-sac tenderness
Dyschezia or cyclic rectal bleeding → bowel involvement; urinary cyclic symptoms → bladder disease
Pain severity poorly correlates with lesion burden; examination may be normal

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Estrogen-responsive implants provoke inflammation, fibrosis, adhesions, and distortion of pelvic anatomy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical assessment + **transvaginal ultrasound** first; normal imaging cannot exclude superficial disease
MRI maps deep lesions or indeterminate adnexal masses; CA-125 not a diagnostic test
★ **Laparoscopy with biopsy** for uncertain diagnosis, refractory symptoms, or planned operative treatment
Current ACOG approach supports presumptive clinical diagnosis; surgery not required before empiric treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Pain, no immediate pregnancy goal → **NSAID + continuous combined OCP** or progestin
Persistent symptoms → GnRH agonist/antagonist with add-back hormones to limit hypoestrogenic adverse effects
Refractory disease or selected infertility → laparoscopic excision/ablation and adhesiolysis
Endometrioma surgery may reduce ovarian reserve; balance pain, suspicion, size, and fertility goals
Trying to conceive → fertility evaluation; hormonal suppression does not improve spontaneous conception

rows.label: Complications
items: Adhesive infertility, bowel/ureteral obstruction, chronic pain; small increase in clear-cell/endometrioid ovarian cancer
GnRH suppression → hot flashes, bone loss; disease may recur after conservative surgery

rows.label: Prevention
items: Postoperative hormonal suppression reduces pain recurrence when pregnancy not desired; no established primary prevention

rows.label: Mimics
items: Adenomyosis: diffusely enlarged, boggy uterus with heavy bleeding
PID: fever, discharge, cervical motion tenderness; pain less cyclic
Primary dysmenorrhea: normal examination, onset soon after menarche, no structural lesion

table.title: Anatomic forms
rows: Fibrotic nodules involving ligaments, bowel, bladder
Ovarian chocolate cyst; homogeneous ground-glass ultrasound echoes

gonococcal-infection.name: Gonococcal infection
gonococcal-infection.scope: Urethritis/cervicitis, disseminated gonococcal infection, gonococcal arthritis, neonatal conjunctivitis
gonococcal-infection.core: Neisseria gonorrhoeae causes mucosal infection and can disseminate into a dermatitis-tenosynovitis-arthritis syndrome or purulent septic arthritis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: New/multiple partners, inconsistent barriers, prior STI, younger age
Complement deficiency increases dissemination risk; neonatal exposure during vaginal delivery

rows.label: Clues
items: Dysuria, mucopurulent discharge, friable cervix; rectal/pharyngeal disease often asymptomatic
★ **Migratory arthralgia, tenosynovitis, sparse pustules** → disseminated infection
Neonate: copious purulent conjunctivitis 2–5 days after birth; corneal injury can progress rapidly

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Gram-negative intracellular diplococci adhere to mucosa; antigenic variation permits recurrent infection
Ascending genital spread or bacteremia extends disease beyond initial exposure site

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **NAAT at exposed sites**: urine/vaginal, rectal, pharyngeal; test chlamydia, HIV, syphilis
Symptomatic male urethral Gram stain may show intracellular diplococci; less reliable at other sites
Dissemination: blood/synovial cultures and mucosal NAAT; negative joint culture does not exclude diagnosis
Suspected treatment failure → culture and antimicrobial susceptibility, assess reinfection

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Uncomplicated: **ceftriaxone 500 mg IM once**; ≥150 kg → 1 g once
Chlamydia not excluded → doxycycline for 7 days; pregnancy → azithromycin instead
★ Disseminated disease → **IV/IM ceftriaxone**, hospitalization initially; drain purulent joint
Neonatal infection → systemic ceftriaxone, or cefotaxime if bilirubin/calcium concerns; topical treatment alone insufficient

rows.label: Complications
items: PID, infertility, ectopic pregnancy, epididymitis, corneal perforation
Rare endocarditis/meningitis; untreated septic arthritis damages cartilage

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Treat partners from preceding **60 days**; abstain 7 days after treatment and until partners treated
Retest at 3 months; pharyngeal test-of-cure at 7–14 days; routine urogenital test-of-cure unnecessary
Condoms, risk-based screening; neonatal erythromycin eye ointment prevents gonococcal ophthalmia

rows.label: Mimics
items: Chlamydia: similar urethritis/cervicitis, NAAT distinguishes
Reactive arthritis: sterile arthritis after infection, conjunctivitis/enthesitis
Staphylococcal arthritis: usually isolated hot joint without migratory skin-tendon syndrome

group-b-streptococcus-prophylaxis.name: Group B streptococcus prophylaxis
group-b-streptococcus-prophylaxis.scope: Universal rectovaginal screening (36-37 weeks), intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis indications (prior infant with GBS, bacteriuria, unknown status with fever, ROM >=18h, <37 weeks), IV penicillin G, penicillin allergy
group-b-streptococcus-prophylaxis.core: Intrapartum antibiotics reduce early-onset neonatal GBS disease in colonized patients and those with specified obstetric risk factors.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ All pregnancies: culture; prior affected infant or current **GBS bacteriuria** → automatic prophylaxis

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Screen **36+0–37+6 weeks**; result generally valid 5 weeks
Begin antibiotics at labor or membrane rupture; aim ≥4 hours exposure without delaying delivery

rows.label: Test
items: **Rectovaginal culture**; request clindamycin susceptibility with serious penicillin allergy

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ Positive culture → **IV penicillin G**; ampicillin acceptable
Unknown status + <37 weeks, temperature ≥38°C, or ROM ≥18 hours → prophylaxis
Suspected intra-amniotic infection → broad-spectrum antibiotics including GBS coverage

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Planned prelabor cesarean with **intact membranes** → no GBS prophylaxis, regardless of culture
GBS bacteriuria ≥100,000 CFU/mL or symptomatic UTI also needs antepartum treatment
Antepartum eradication of asymptomatic vaginal colonization does not replace intrapartum antibiotics

herpes-simplex-virus.name: Herpes simplex virus
herpes-simplex-virus.scope: HSV-1 and HSV-2, genital herpes, neonatal herpes, herpes labialis, eczema herpeticum, acyclovir
herpes-simplex-virus.core: Painful grouped vesicles recurring at mucocutaneous sites reflect latent HSV reactivation; neonatal infection and disseminated disease require urgent systemic treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Skin/mucosal contact, asymptomatic shedding, new sexual partners; either HSV type can cause genital disease
Immunosuppression, atopic dermatitis; neonatal risk highest with newly acquired maternal infection near delivery

rows.label: Clues
items: Primary genital episode: fever, tender nodes, dysuria, multiple painful ulcers; recurrences generally milder
Labialis: tingling prodrome around lip; herpetic whitlow: painful finger vesicles
★ **Monomorphic punched-out erosions in eczema** → eczema herpeticum; ocular symptoms threaten vision
Neonate: sepsislike illness, vesicles sometimes absent; seizures/hepatitis suggest CNS or disseminated disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: HSV establishes sensory ganglion latency; stress, illness, UV exposure trigger reactivation
Genital HSV-2 recurs and sheds more frequently than genital HSV-1

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Active lesion → **HSV PCR/NAAT with typing**; culture less sensitive as lesions heal
CSF HSV PCR for encephalitis/neonatal CNS concern; early negative may require repeat testing
Neonate → lesion/surface, blood, CSF testing plus liver enzymes; start treatment while testing
Type-specific serology only selected situations; no routine population screening or HSV IgM

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ First genital episode → **oral acyclovir or valacyclovir for 7–10 days**
Recurrence → prompt episodic dosing at prodrome; frequent/distressing episodes → daily suppressive valacyclovir
★ Neonatal, CNS, disseminated disease or severe eczema herpeticum → **IV acyclovir**; neonatal duration below
Genital HSV pregnancy: suppress acyclovir/valacyclovir from 36 weeks; lesions/prodrome at labor → cesarean
Corneal involvement → urgent ophthalmology; avoid unsupervised ocular corticosteroids

rows.label: Complications
items: Encephalitis, aseptic meningitis, urinary retention, keratitis, dissemination; increased HIV acquisition risk
Acyclovir → crystal nephropathy, neurotoxicity with renal impairment; hydration and dose adjustment

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Avoid sex during lesions/prodrome**, condoms, partner disclosure; suppression lowers but never eliminates transmission
Avoid kissing infants with active labialis; cover lesions, hand hygiene

rows.label: Mimics
items: Syphilis: classically painless chancre
Aphthae: mucosal ulcers without preceding grouped vesicles
Zoster: unilateral dermatomal eruption rather than recurrent focal mucocutaneous clusters

herpes-simplex-virus.evidence: Checked genital disease 2026-10-30: [CDC HSV guidance](https://www.cdc.gov/std/treatment-guidelines/herpes.htm); neonatal/eczema management established teaching.

table.title: Neonatal IV acyclovir duration
rows: ≥21 days; CNS: confirm CSF PCR clearance

hypertensive-disorders-of-pregnancy.name: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy
hypertensive-disorders-of-pregnancy.scope: Chronic and gestational HTN, preeclampsia, HELLP, eclampsia
hypertensive-disorders-of-pregnancy.core: Pregnancy-associated hypertension; maternal organ injury or placental dysfunction signals danger even without substantial proteinuria.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior preeclampsia, chronic HTN, CKD, diabetes, SLE/APS, multifetal gestation
Nulliparity, obesity, age ≥35, family history

rows.label: Clues
items: Headache, visual disturbance, RUQ/epigastric pain, dyspnea; edema nonspecific
★ Severe features: **platelets <100,000/µL**, creatinine >1.1 mg/dL or doubled, transaminases ≥2× normal
Other severe features: pulmonary edema, refractory neurologic symptoms
Presentation through **6 weeks postpartum**; eclampsia/HELLP possible without prior HTN

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Abnormal spiral-artery remodeling → placental ischemia → systemic endothelial injury, vasospasm, capillary leak

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **BP ≥140/90**, either component, twice ≥4 h apart; severe ≥160/110 confirmed within minutes
CBC/platelets, creatinine, AST/ALT, urine protein; fetal growth US + antenatal testing
Proteinuria: **≥300 mg/24 h** or protein/creatinine ≥0.3; dipstick 2+ only if quantification unavailable
Chronic HTN + new proteinuria/end-organ injury → superimposed preeclampsia; HELLP: smear, LDH ≥600 IU/L

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Persistent severe BP ≥15 min → **IV labetalol/hydralazine** or immediate-release oral nifedipine within 30–60 min
★ Severe preeclampsia/eclampsia → **magnesium sulfate** through 24 h postpartum; airway before delivery
Chronic HTN ≥140/90 → oral labetalol/extended-release nifedipine; avoid ACE inhibitors/ARBs
Mg toxicity: areflexia/hypoventilation → stop infusion, **IV calcium gluconate**; oliguria → reduce dose

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, abruption, DIC, AKI, hepatic hematoma/rupture; fetal growth restriction, prematurity, death

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ High risk or multiple moderate risks → **aspirin 81 mg/day**, start 12–28 wk, ideally before 16
Postpartum BP review within 72 h if severe, otherwise 7–10 days; long-term cardiovascular follow-up

rows.label: Mimics
items: TTP: profound thrombocytopenia/hemolysis, persists after delivery
Acute fatty liver: hypoglycemia, jaundice, marked coagulopathy
Epilepsy: established seizure disorder; evaluate alternative causes despite obstetric context

table.title: Classification and delivery
rows: Before 20 wk or persists >12 wk postpartum
After 20 wk + proteinuria OR severe features
Severe BP alone sufficient; <34 stable → betamethasone
Hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelets
Deliver after stabilization, any gestational age

hyperthyroidism.name: Hyperthyroidism and thyrotoxicosis
hyperthyroidism.scope: Graves disease, toxic multinodular goiter, toxic adenoma, subacute thyroiditis, thyroid storm, beta-blockers, thionamides, radioactive iodine
hyperthyroidism.core: Excess circulating thyroid hormone → heat intolerance, weight loss despite appetite, tremor, and tachycardia; hormone overproduction differs from destructive release.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autoimmune history, female sex; older age favors autonomous nodules
Iodine load, amiodarone, exogenous thyroid hormone; infection/surgery can precipitate storm

rows.label: Clues
items: Hyperreflexia, frequent stools, proximal weakness, widened pulse pressure; older adults may have apathetic presentation
★ **Thyroid storm**: fever, delirium, severe tachyarrhythmia, vomiting, heart failure; clinical diagnosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Increased tissue metabolic activity and beta-adrenergic sensitivity explain systemic manifestations
Thionamides block thyroid peroxidase; PTU also reduces peripheral T4 → T3 conversion

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **TSH first → free T4**, total T3 if T4 normal; suppressed TSH with elevated hormones
TRAb establishes Graves; uncertain cause → radioactive iodine uptake, except pregnancy/lactation
Low uptake: thyroiditis/exogenous hormone; low thyroglobulin supports exogenous ingestion

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptom control: **propranolol**; caution in asthma or decompensated HF
★ Storm → ICU, cooling/fluids, beta-blockade if tolerated, **PTU → iodine ≥1 hour later**, hydrocortisone
Radioiodine contraindicated during pregnancy/lactation; significant active orbitopathy favors another definitive treatment
Compression/suspicious nodule → thyroidectomy after control; pregnancy: first-trimester PTU, later methimazole

rows.label: Complications
items: AF, embolism, osteoporosis, cardiomyopathy; radioiodine often → hypothyroidism
★ Thionamides: **fever/sore throat → stop drug, urgent CBC**; PTU → severe hepatotoxicity

rows.label: Prevention
items: Monitor free T4 early during treatment; TSH recovery lags
Smoking cessation for orbitopathy; definitive treatment before planned pregnancy when feasible

rows.label: Mimics
items: Panic disorder: episodic symptoms without thyroid biochemical abnormalities
Pheochromocytoma: paroxysmal headache, sweating, severe hypertension
Menopause: hot flashes with menstrual transition, normal thyroid testing

table.title: Etiology determines treatment
rows: Diffuse uptake; bruit, orbitopathy, pretibial myxedema
One hot nodule, suppressed surrounding tissue
NSAID; prednisone if severe; no thionamides

intra-amniotic-infection.name: Intra-amniotic infection
intra-amniotic-infection.scope: Chorioamnionitis, clinical diagnostic criteria (maternal fever, fetal tachycardia, purulent fluid, uterine tenderness), IV ampicillin and gentamicin, labor augmentation, postpartum endometritis
intra-amniotic-infection.core: Intrapartum fever with fetal tachycardia or purulent cervical drainage suggests ascending infection requiring antibiotics and delivery.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prolonged membrane rupture, prolonged labor, repeated digital examinations after rupture, internal monitoring
Genital tract colonization; infection can occur with intact membranes

rows.label: Clues
items: Uterine tenderness, foul amniotic fluid, maternal tachycardia, leukocytosis
Hypotension, altered mentation, oliguria → maternal sepsis; leukocytosis alone nonspecific during labor

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Polymicrobial ascent from vagina into decidua, membranes, amniotic fluid, and fetus

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected infection: temperature **≥39°C**, or **38–38.9°C plus one additional clinical risk factor**
Additional factors: fetal baseline >160/min, purulent cervical drainage, maternal leukocytosis without corticosteroids
ACOG 2024 permits diagnosis without fever when other clinical findings strongly support infection
Clinical diagnosis; placental histology or amniotic-fluid testing confirms retrospectively; never delay treatment
Sepsis → blood cultures, lactate, CBC, renal function; cultures before antibiotics only without delay

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Prompt **IV ampicillin + gentamicin**, acetaminophen, IV fluids; notify neonatal team
★ Induce/augment labor with **oxytocin**; infection alone is not a cesarean indication
Cesarean for obstetric indication → add clindamycin for anaerobic coverage; postpartum dosing depends on course
Shock → fluid resuscitation, norepinephrine, urgent source control; do not await fetal lung maturity

rows.label: Complications
items: Uterine atony/hemorrhage, postpartum endometritis, bacteremia, septic shock
Neonatal pneumonia, sepsis, meningitis; prematurity-related morbidity

rows.label: Prevention
items: Minimize digital examinations after rupture; timely term-PROM induction; PPROM latency antibiotics when expectant

rows.label: Mimics
items: Epidural-associated fever: sterile inflammation possible; cannot dismiss coexisting infection
★ Postpartum endometritis: fever and fundal tenderness after birth → **clindamycin + gentamicin**
Pyelonephritis: flank tenderness and positive urine culture

intra-amniotic-infection.evidence: Diagnostic update checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG 2024](https://doi.org/10.1097/aog.0000000000005593); management follows established ACOG teaching.

intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.name: Intrapartum fetal monitoring
intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.scope: Baseline fetal heart rate, variability, early decelerations, late decelerations, variable decelerations, category I II III tracings, intrauterine resuscitation
intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.core: Fetal oxygenation assessment from baseline, variability, and decelerations; persistent category III requires expedited delivery after immediate resuscitation.

rows.label: Definition
items: ★ Normal baseline **110–160/min**; moderate variability **6–25 beats/min**
Bradycardia <110; tachycardia >160; baseline change lasts ≥10 minutes
Tachysystole: >5 contractions/10 minutes, averaged over 30 minutes

rows.label: Interpret
items: Early: mirrors contraction → head compression; benign
Late: nadir after contraction peak → uteroplacental insufficiency
Variable: abrupt fall → cord compression; prolonged: 2–10 minutes

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Category II: lateral positioning, stop oxytocin, IV fluids; correct hypotension
Persistent tachysystole with concerning tracing → **terbutaline**; recurrent variables → amnioinfusion
★ Sustained bradycardia → vaginal examination for prolapsed cord; prepare urgent delivery

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Oxygen only for **maternal hypoxemia**; older routine-oxygen answers conflict with current guidance
Moderate variability or accelerations strongly argues against current metabolic acidemia
Category II alone does not mandate cesarean; reassess response and labor progress

table.title: Three-tier interpretation
rows: Reassuring rate/variability; no late or variable decelerations
Absent variability + recurrent late/variable decelerations or bradycardia
Evaluate severe anemia; expedite if persistent

neural-tube-defects.name: Neural tube defects
neural-tube-defects.scope: Anencephaly, spina bifida occulta, meningocele, myelomeningocele, Chiari II malformation, maternal serum AFP, amniotic acetylcholinesterase, lemon and banana signs, folic acid prevention
neural-tube-defects.core: Neural tube closure failure by approximately 4 weeks after conception produces cranial or spinal defects; prevention must begin before pregnancy recognition.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Low folate, prior affected pregnancy, maternal diabetes/obesity, valproate/carbamazepine, early-pregnancy hyperthermia

rows.label: Clues
items: Midline lumbosacral sac, lower-limb weakness, absent reflexes, bladder dysfunction with neural involvement
★ **Lemon skull and banana cerebellum** on fetal ultrasound suggest open spina bifida/Chiari II
Occult lesions: hair tuft, atypical deep dimple, hemangioma; normal skin does not guarantee normal cord

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Failed neurulation leaves neural tissue unprotected; CSF leakage contributes to hindbrain herniation
Folate supports nucleotide synthesis during rapid embryonic cell division

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Maternal serum **AFP at 15–22 weeks**; elevation → verify dating/number, detailed ultrasound
Open defects elevate AFP; closed occulta may not; cfDNA does not screen neural tube defects
★ Uncertain imaging → amniotic fluid **AFP and acetylcholinesterase**; target anatomy scan at 18–22 weeks
Postnatal spinal ultrasound in young infant or MRI for suspected occult dysraphism/tethered cord

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Open spinal lesion: **prone positioning, sterile saline dressing**, avoid pressure/contamination; neonatal neurosurgery
Early closure; assess hydrocephalus, renal function and bladder emptying; intermittent catheterization when neurogenic
Selected prenatal myelomeningocele repair can improve motor outcomes/reduce shunting, with maternal and prematurity risks
Anencephaly → counseling, pregnancy options, and palliative neonatal care; no curative treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Hydrocephalus, Chiari II, meningitis, orthopedic deformities, neurogenic bowel/bladder, recurrent UTI and kidney injury
Tethered cord may cause progressive weakness or continence changes during growth

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Folic acid 400–800 µg/day** before conception through early pregnancy for average risk
Prior NTD pregnancy → **4 mg/day**, starting ≥1 month before conception through first 3 months
Optimize diabetes, review antiseizure drugs before pregnancy; avoid prolonged overheating

rows.label: Mimics
items: Sacrococcygeal teratoma: solid/cystic mass, not exposed neural placode
Abdominal wall defect: elevated AFP but bowel outside abdomen on ultrasound

table.title: Lesions
rows: Meninges/CSF herniate; cord remains within canal

neural-tube-defects.evidence: Folate checked 2026-10-30: [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/folic-acid/hcp/clinical-overview/), [USPSTF 2023](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/document/ClinicalSummaryFinal/folic-acid-for-the-prevention-of-neural-tube-defects-preventive-medication); remaining content established teaching.

normal-and-abnormal-labor.name: Normal and abnormal labor
normal-and-abnormal-labor.scope: Latent vs active first stage, second stage, active phase protraction and arrest (oxytocin, cesarean), false labor (Braxton Hicks), operative vaginal delivery, labor induction
normal-and-abnormal-labor.core: True labor produces progressive cervical change; dystocia management depends on stage, contraction adequacy, fetal status, and descent.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Nulliparity, obesity, fetal macrosomia, malposition, cephalopelvic disproportion, inadequate uterine contractions

rows.label: Clues
items: Assess membrane status, presentation, fetal heart tracing, serial dilation, station, and maternal vital signs
★ Tachysystole: **>5 contractions/10 minutes**, averaged over 30 minutes

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Dysfunctional powers, passenger, or passage → delayed dilation or descent

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Active arrest requires ruptured membranes: no change after **4 hours adequate** or 6 hours inadequate contractions
Adequate activity: ≥200 Montevideo units; intrauterine pressure catheter when external assessment insufficient
Prolonged pushing: >3 hours nulliparous, >2 hours multiparous; individualize by descent and fetal status
Failed induction requires ≥12–18 hours oxytocin after ROM; slow latent phase alone does not mandate cesarean

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Protraction with weak contractions → **oxytocin**, amniotomy; established active arrest → cesarean
Tachysystole → stop oxytocin, lateral positioning; persistent fetal compromise → terbutaline, expedited delivery
★ Operative vaginal birth requires full dilation, ruptured membranes, engaged head, known position, skilled operator
Unfavorable cervix → balloon or prostaglandin ripening, then oxytocin; avoid misoprostol after prior cesarean
Avoid vacuum before 34 weeks or with face presentation; failed operative attempt → cesarean

rows.label: Complications
items: Maternal infection, hemorrhage, exhaustion; neonatal hypoxia
Forceps/vacuum → maternal lacerations, neonatal scalp injury; vacuum → subgaleal hemorrhage

rows.label: Prevention
items: Induce for maternal/fetal indications or offer elective induction from 39 weeks; no elective earlier delivery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Braxton Hicks: irregular contractions without cervical change
Obstructed labor: adequate contractions without progress; augmentation cannot correct mechanical obstruction

polycystic-ovary-syndrome.name: Polycystic ovary syndrome
polycystic-ovary-syndrome.scope: Rotterdam criteria (hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, polycystic ovaries), metabolic risks, weight loss, oral contraceptives, ovulation induction (letrozole, clomiphene)
polycystic-ovary-syndrome.core: Hyperandrogenism and chronic ovulatory dysfunction after exclusion of alternative causes suggest PCOS; management follows metabolic, menstrual and fertility priorities.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, insulin resistance and obesity; lean patients can also have PCOS
Pubertal transition can mimic disease, requiring stricter adolescent diagnostic criteria

rows.label: Clues
items: Irregular/infrequent menses, infertility, hirsutism, acne or androgenic alopecia
Acanthosis nigricans suggests hyperinsulinemia; obesity is supportive, not required
Rapid virilization, deep voice or markedly elevated androgens → investigate tumor rather than assume PCOS

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Insulin resistance and ovarian androgen excess impair follicular maturation and ovulation
Absent cyclic progesterone permits persistent estrogen-driven endometrial proliferation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Adults: **2 of 3 Rotterdam** features—hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, polycystic ovarian morphology
Exclude mimics: **hCG, TSH, prolactin, morning 17-hydroxyprogesterone**; latter screens nonclassic CAH
Total/free testosterone for biochemical androgen assessment; DHEAS if adrenal source suspected
★ Irregular cycles plus hyperandrogenism → **ultrasound not required**; LH:FSH ratio not diagnostic
BP, lipid profile and **oral glucose tolerance test** assess metabolic risk; adolescent diagnosis avoids ultrasound criteria

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Lifestyle/weight management for all; modest weight loss can restore ovulation in overweight patients
★ No pregnancy desired → **combined OCP** for cycles/androgen symptoms; cyclic progestin or LNG-IUD protects endometrium
Persistent hirsutism → spironolactone with reliable contraception; allow months for hair response
Metabolic risk/insulin resistance → metformin; less effective than OCP for androgen symptoms
★ Anovulatory infertility → **letrozole first-line**; clomiphene alternative after evaluating other infertility factors

rows.label: Complications
items: Endometrial hyperplasia/cancer, infertility, type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, OSA and depression
Pregnancy → increased gestational diabetes and hypertensive-disorder risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: Regular progestin exposure for prolonged amenorrhea; persistent abnormal bleeding → endometrial assessment
Periodic glycemic/BP/lipid reassessment; preconception metabolic optimization and folate

rows.label: Mimics
items: Androgen-secreting tumor: rapid progression, severe virilization
Nonclassic CAH: elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone
Functional hypothalamic amenorrhea: low estrogen with exercise/energy deficit

postoperative-fever.name: Postoperative fever
postoperative-fever.scope: Timing (Wind, Water, Wound, Walking, Wonder drugs), atelectasis, surgical site infection, intra-abdominal abscess
postoperative-fever.core: Fever after surgery: postoperative interval narrows causes; hemodynamic instability or focal findings determine urgency, testing, and source control.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Emergency or contaminated surgery, bowel anastomosis, diabetes, immunosuppression
Prolonged ventilation, urinary catheters, central lines, immobility; new medications or transfusion

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Shock, rapidly spreading wound pain, crepitus** → invasive infection regardless of postoperative day
Purulent drainage, dysuria, productive cough, hypoxemia, or abdominal tenderness localize the source
Persistent ileus, leukocytosis, recurrent fever after initial improvement → intra-abdominal collection

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inflammatory cytokines arise from sterile injury or infection; later onset raises infection probability
**Atelectasis does not establish the cause of fever**; historical Wind attribution lacks supporting evidence

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Examine first**: incision, lungs, abdomen, lines, urine symptoms, legs; timing alone never diagnoses
Stable isolated fever within 48 hours → observation; avoid reflex cultures or antibiotics
Focal findings → chest radiograph, urinalysis/culture, or wound culture; sepsis → blood cultures and lactate
★ Suspected deep abdominal infection → **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast**

rows.label: Tx
items: Sepsis → IV crystalloids, broad antibiotics, urgent source control; do not delay for imaging
Superficial incisional abscess → open/drain; add antibiotics for cellulitis or systemic illness
★ Intra-abdominal abscess → **percutaneous drainage + piperacillin-tazobactam**; anastomotic leak/peritonitis → surgery
Pulmonary collapse → analgesia, mobilization, lung expansion; suspected drug fever → stop culprit

rows.label: Complications
items: Septic shock, dehiscence, organ failure; missed anastomotic leak → diffuse peritonitis
Unnecessary antimicrobials → C difficile, resistance; immobilization → VTE

rows.label: Prevention
items: Preincision antibiotic prophylaxis, aseptic technique, glucose control; promptly remove unnecessary catheters
Early ambulation, pulmonary hygiene, mechanical/pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis when bleeding risk permits

rows.label: Mimics
items: Malignant hyperthermia: perioperative rigidity, rapidly rising end-tidal CO2, hyperthermia
Transfusion reaction: fever temporally linked to blood administration; stop transfusion immediately

table.title: Timing: clues, not diagnostic rules
rows: Sterile inflammation; aspiration; dangerous early wound infection
Walking: VTE; Wonder drugs: drug fever

postoperative-fever.evidence: Atelectasis evidence checked 2026-10-30: [Chest systematic review, 2011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21527508/); remaining management: established surgical teaching.

postpartum-care.name: Postpartum care
postpartum-care.scope: Normal puerperal changes, lochia, uterine involution, perineal and cesarean wound healing, breastfeeding, postpartum depression screening, routine postpartum visit
postpartum-care.core: Postpartum care is an ongoing assessment of recovery, mood, infant feeding, contraception, and chronic disease after every birth.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ All postpartum patients; assess support, sleep, safety, sexual health, and reproductive goals

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Contact within **3 weeks**; comprehensive visit by **12 weeks**, with earlier risk-based review
Hypertensive disorder → BP within 7–10 days; severe hypertension → within 72 hours

rows.label: Test
items: ★ Edinburgh or PHQ-9 depression screen; assess suicidality directly after positive self-harm response
BP, bleeding, fundal tenderness; inspect perineum/incision for erythema, drainage, separation
Observe latch/milk transfer; frequent feeds, lactation support; cracked nipples → correct positioning

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ Heavy bleeding, fever, dyspnea, severe headache → urgent evaluation
Mood screen positive → diagnostic interview, psychotherapy/SSRI; psychosis → emergency hospitalization
Increasing wound pain/purulence → evaluate infection; breast fluctuance → ultrasound for abscess

rows.label: Traps
items: Ovulation may precede first period; discuss contraception before discharge
Lactational contraception: amenorrhea, exclusive frequent breastfeeding, infant <6 months
Postpartum hypertension and cardiomyopathy can first appear after discharge

table.title: Expected recovery
rows: Descends daily; near prepregnancy size by 6 weeks
Pain progressively improves; keep clean, monitor healing
Early cramping and fluid loss; breastfeeding intensifies cramping

postpartum-care.evidence: Visit timing checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG postpartum care](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2018/05/optimizing-postpartum-care); normal physiology established teaching.

postpartum-hemorrhage.name: Postpartum hemorrhage
postpartum-hemorrhage.scope: Primary postpartum hemorrhage (uterine atony, lacerations, retained placenta, coagulopathy), secondary postpartum hemorrhage (retained products of conception, endometritis), barrier methods, surgical management
postpartum-hemorrhage.core: Excessive bleeding after delivery demands simultaneous resuscitation and cause-directed control: Tone, Trauma, Tissue and Thrombin.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Uterine overdistention, prolonged/augmented labor, chorioamnionitis, magnesium, prior PPH → atony
Operative delivery → trauma; placenta accreta/retention → tissue; abruption/sepsis → coagulopathy

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Boggy enlarged uterus** → atony; firm uterus with bleeding → laceration or other cause
Incomplete placenta → retained tissue; diffuse oozing → coagulopathy
Shock out of proportion to visible loss → concealed hematoma or inversion
Delayed bleeding >24 hours to weeks postpartum → retained products, endometritis or subinvolution

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Myometrial contraction compresses placental-bed vessels; failed contraction or disrupted tissue prevents hemostasis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Quantify blood loss; US definition **≥1000 mL or hypovolemia within 24 hours**, regardless of route
WHO 2025 earlier treatment trigger: ≥500 mL, or ≥300 mL with abnormal hemodynamic signs
Assess uterine tone, inspect birth canal/placenta; CBC, coagulation studies, fibrinogen and crossmatch
Ultrasound for suspected retained products; avoid delaying control in active unstable bleeding

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Hemorrhage team, two large IVs, warmed balanced blood resuscitation; massage, empty bladder, **oxytocin**
★ **Tranexamic acid within 3 hours** alongside first-response treatment
Refractory atony → **balloon/vacuum**, embolization if stable; compression sutures/arterial ligation or hysterectomy
Laceration → repair; retained tissue → evacuation; inversion → manual replacement before uterotonics
Endometritis → **clindamycin + gentamicin**

rows.label: Complications
items: DIC, AKI, shock, death; severe ischemia → Sheehan syndrome
Transfusion complications and hysterectomy-related fertility loss; delayed anemia impairs recovery

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Prophylactic **oxytocin after delivery**, active third-stage management and antenatal anemia treatment
Risk assessment, blood availability and team readiness; routine prophylactic TXA not recommended for vaginal birth

rows.label: Mimics
